title: LOCAL DELIVERY (GOPUFF)
subtitle: It looks like an ordering system, but most of the load is people checking what is available near them.
footer: DDIA: Ch 7 conditional updates · Ch 5 replica lag   ·   Similar: URL shortener · Rate limiter · Business discovery · News feed

items: Browsing availability is far more frequent than ordering, so cache it and serve it from replicas.
Find nearby warehouses with an in-memory list and a cheap distance filter before calling any travel-time API.
Prevent overselling with conditional stock decrements for every item in one transaction.
Check availability of items deliverable to a location (DCs within 1 hour)
Order multiple items; never sell stock you don't have
Availability p99 < 100ms
Orders strongly consistent (no overselling)
10k distribution centres (DCs), ~100k SKUs
Browse load ≫ order load
Orders ~1M/day ≈ 12/s.
The DC list (10k rows) fits in memory.

Naive: call a travel-time API for every DC. 10k calls per page view is far too slow.

items: Keep the small DC list in memory, prefilter by straight-line distance, then ask travel time for only a handful of candidates.
Browse reads come from a short-TTL cache and read replicas. Slightly stale is fine here (AP).
Ordering hits the primary: one transaction with UPDATE … SET qty = qty − n WHERE qty ≥ n per item.
How do you prevent overselling?
A conditional decrement per item inside one transaction; row locks serialize concurrent buyers.
Stale availability vs orders?
Different consistency per path: browse is cached and eventually consistent; checkout reads and writes the primary.
Scale orders?
Partition inventory by region; an order only touches nearby DCs, so there are no cross-shard transactions.
Hot item (flash sale)?
Row contention on one inventory row: queue orders per item, or split stock into sub-buckets.
Redis as the inventory source of truth, with no multi-item transaction or durability.
Adding parts before a number shows they are needed.
Ignoring retries, timeouts and crashes.
